props.title: Ray
props.initialSlug: Ray Charles' journey from blind boy to soul legend

sections.content: Ray (2004) revolutionized the musical biopic through Jamie Foxx's transformative performance as Ray Charles. Unlike sanitized predecessors like The Glenn Miller Story (1954), Ray confronts Charles' heroin addiction, infidelity, and complex relationship with his mother head-on. The film's innovative structure weaves childhood trauma with adult success, showing how Charles' early blindness and brother's death shaped his music. Director Taylor Hackford captures the evolution of R&B through the 1950s and 60s, particularly in electric performance sequences of "What'd I Say" and "Georgia On My Mind."

sections.content: The success of Ray sparked a renaissance in music biopics that weren't afraid to show artists' flaws. Bohemian Rhapsody (2018) and Rocketman (2019) followed its template of balancing spectacular performance sequences with personal struggles. But Ray's greatest achievement is depicting Charles' innovation in breaking down racial and genre barriers, especially in his controversial move from gospel to secular music and later embrace of country western.

The film excels in showing how Charles' disability became his strength, with vivid sound design putting viewers inside his heightened auditory world. This influenced later disability portrayals in films like Sound of Metal (2019) and Music of Silence (2017). Jamie Foxx's Oscar-winning performance set a new standard for actor transformations, going beyond mere imitation to capture Charles' essence. SUBHEAD: Musical Innovation and Social Impact

movies.title: La Vie en Rose
movies.slug: Marion Cotillard's stunning portrayal of Edith Piaf redefined what was possible in biographical performance

sections.content: Ray Charles' boundary-breaking fusion of gospel, R&B, country and pop is carefully documented, showing how he helped create soul music. The film's depiction of segregation-era touring and Charles' eventual refusal to play segregated venues in Georgia makes it as much a civil rights document as a musical biography. This influenced later films like Selma (2014) and One Night in Miami (2020) in showing how artists became activists.
